Betterleaks image for the CI secret-scan task. Kept in lockstep with the betterleaks rev in .pre-commit-config.yaml by the betterleaks group below; the .tektonic/** postUpgradeTasks re-synthesize .tekton/.

alpine/k8s image for the CI check tasks. Lives in .tektonic/pipeline.ts so the bump happens at the source; the .tektonic/** postUpgradeTasks re-synthesize .tekton/. Grouped with alpine/kubectl as k8s-tools.

CloudNativePG Cluster images. The kubernetes manager only reads image:, so spec.imageName needs its own matcher. The docker tag suffix (e.g. -standard-trixie) keeps the image flavour and OS fixed across updates.

packageRules.description: Vendored upstream release manifests. Each is one file carrying the CRDs, RBAC and ConfigMaps for a single version alongside its image tags, so bumping the tags in place leaves new binaries on old CRDs — which is exactly what happened to pipelines-as-code (v0.51.0 images, v0.48.0 CRDs) and to tekton pipelines, whose injected entrypoint image the manager cannot even see. Renovate tracks the *_VERSION pins in the update-manifests.sh scripts instead (see customManagers), and CI enforces that the manifest matches.

Re-synthesize .tekton/ on any branch that touches .tektonic/ (a @tektonic-ci/core bump or any other .tektonic dependency). Without this the PR carries the new library but the old manifests. Needs RENOVATE_ALLOWED_COMMANDS on the renovate-homelab cronjob. installTools makes node available whatever manager produced the branch; executionMode 'branch' runs the synth once over the final set of updates.

Re-vendor the manifests on any branch that bumps a *_VERSION pin in an update-manifests.sh (see customManagers). Without this the PR carries the new pin but the old manifest, and check-vendored-manifests.sh fails it. All three scripts run unconditionally: tekton updates share one grouped branch, and executionMode 'branch' runs the commands once with no per-update templating, so a script whose pin did not move just rewrites identical files. uv and python are for the PAC script's second-controller.py. Needs RENOVATE_ALLOWED_COMMANDS on the renovate-homelab cronjob.
The local pre-commit hook and the CI secret-scan task must run the same scanner version, or a commit that passes locally can fail CI (or worse, the reverse).
A Postgres major needs a backup, CNPG's pg_upgrade path and matching ocidex test images, so it is done by hand rather than by a Renovate PR.
Majors only get a PR once approved on the Dependency Dashboard.

Grafana/Prometheus charts move together and break together. Weekly so the near-daily chart releases land as one PR. The window holds two renovate-homelab runs (01:00 and 05:00 Monday, see cronjob.yaml) in case one is missed.
Renovate ships almost daily; one bump a week is enough.
Both track the Kubernetes release (see K8S_TOOLS in .tektonic/pipeline.ts).

Automerge low-risk minor/patch updates once the PAC check passes (GitHub native auto-merge, so they merge without waiting for the next Renovate run). The release must be 3 days old first; timestamp-optional so OCI artifacts without a publish time are not held back forever. Not here on purpose: cilium, fluxcd, talos/kubernetes (can take down the cluster or GitOps), tekton/pipelines-as-code (they run the CI that gates the merge), postgres images (restart the database), and all majors.
Patch-only automerge: cloudnative-pg operator chart and the CI tool images.
tsidp is pre-1.0 and its grant schema and env names still change between patch releases; every bump needs a read of the release notes.
Under 0.x a minor bump is allowed to break things (synology-csi, local-path-provisioner), so those stay manual.
